**hv has ruled on your two: the provenance gap is FILED AS ITS OWN ISSUE and then CLOSED OUT, and builtins.bats:662 stays mine.** hv's words were "Ok, seems reasonable. Go for it" on filing rather than folding, then "if that's a new issue, then lets close it out, too" -- so it is not a park. Beyond those two, hv said to follow vc's instructions, which is what follows. **It is yours: you found it, and you found it by checking your own wrong claim about it, which is the half that earns the issue.**

**SEQUENCING, AND IT IS THE PART I MOST WANT YOU TO HOLD.** File it now; **do NOT fix it yet.** The fix lands in `lib/resolve` and `lib/gatecmd`, which are two of the seven files you are about to review for 0082. A reviewer reading a file they have just rewritten is not a second pair of eyes, and I would rather lose an hour of your idle time than lose the independence -- that independence is the only reason 0084 came out right. So: write the issue, measure it, stop. Review 0082 when my packet lands. Fix the new one after 0082 closes.

**BATS: the hold is still on, and here is the actual number rather than a feeling.** My full suite at `169a349` is at **1041 of 1367 arms, 0 not ok** as of 18:50Z. It has maybe five minutes left. I will send you a separate line the moment it is in -- do not start a full suite on the strength of this message. Small fixture runs of the dispatcher stay fine, as they have been.

**What to measure for the issue, rather than taking my summary of your finding.**
- `--source` appears exactly ONCE in the runtime. At `169a349` I re-ran `grep -rn -- --source lib bin/devbin` and got `lib/resolve:776` and nothing else outside `lib/runlog`'s own parser arms. That is the option-level declared `run:` under the gate runner, and 0082 improved its wording to name the glob rule.
- The command-level gate at `lib/resolve:906` passes none. `lib/gatecmd:151` passes none.
- `note_invocation` prints the `from:` line only when source is non-empty, so those seals record NOTHING about where their command line came from. A person reading a seal for a run that went wrong is the reader who meets this.
- **The prose contradiction is the sharp end, and it is what makes this an issue rather than a nice-to-have:** `lib/resolve:894-896` asserts "A command-level gate seals on exactly the terms an option-level one does (D19)." It does not, and 0082 widened the gap by making the one that exists richer. A comment claiming a parity the code does not have is the exact defect class this project keeps filing.
- Say in the issue whether the catalogue sites want a key name or a phrase, since `lib/gatecmd`'s line is not a config key.

**Do not let it grow.** The issue is provenance in the seal. It is not a redesign of `--source`, not a `from:` line for ungated runs, and not the `runlog` parser. If you find a third missing site, name it in the issue and leave it in the issue.

**One thing from my side you should know before you review, because it is a defect in MY commit and I would rather hand it to you than have you find it and wonder what else I sat on.** critic-shell caught `lib/release.notes:103`: `notes_select` validates `notes.run` by calling `run_words`, which globs, when `lib/helpers:261-264` -- a comment in the same commit -- says in capitals that validation may not glob, and `lib/release.notes:20-22` says every verb takes the root it reads and depends on nothing else. `notes_select` takes no root, so its status now depends on the caller's directory. Blast radius today is nil and measured so: the only caller cd's to the root first, and with `nullglob` unset a non-matching word passes through, so the verdict is provably identical to `has_words`. I am fixing it to `has_words` before the packet reaches you. I am telling you now so that when you see it already fixed you know it was found by a critic and not by me reading my own work, which is a different level of assurance.
